correctness.rationale: For any finite binary word, circular one-counts at a fixed length form an integer interval. Its extrema grow by either zero or one as the window length increases. Splitting all windows of the alternating-zero complement morphism by starting parity gives the four exact extrema recurrences; summing odd- and even-length complexities telescopes to \(S(\mu(w))=2S(w)+|w|-|w|_1\). The one-count recurrence of period-doubling iterates then yields the closed formula. All boundary cases including constant words, full traversals, and rank zero are handled. A separate enumeration checks all 510 binary words of lengths 1–8 and the complete spectra at ranks 0–11, but only the proof establishes the infinite claim.

originality.rationale: Two relevant primary articles concern (i) conjugacy classes of factors in the infinite word and (ii) 2-Abelian equivalence or two-block codings in infinite-word factors. Neither theorem as inspected implies a finite-cycle, length-resolved Parikh-class transfer law for arbitrary inputs, or the exact total for every complete finite period-doubling iterate. Comparable previous local findings concern infinite cyclic factor classes, a stronger 2-Abelian relation, a Cantor-word rather than period-doubling circle, or Burrows–Wheeler runs. A 2016 related paper was inspected at abstract level only, so novelty remains qualified.

value.rationale: A finite circular Parikh spectrum is a natural count of all attainable symbol-composition classes at each window length. The result classifies the entire lengthwise spectrum recursively across every rank, and its sum is an exact growing invariant of classical period-doubling words rather than a sample statistic. The arbitrary-input transport theorem exposes the mechanism and yields the first-order summatory identity; the exact all-ranks formula and logarithmic mean growth do not follow merely from knowing the infinite-word Abelian complexity. The result does not claim a downstream application or novelty proof from computation alone.
